question: Which of the following causes of erectile dysfunction reacts with greater sensitivity to intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hormonal -> Erectile dysfunction -> Intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs sensitivity -> 80% CHAIN: Arterial -> Erectile dysfunction -> Intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs sensitivity -> 75% CHAIN: Neurogenic -> Erectile dysfunction -> Intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs sensitivity -> 70% CHAIN: Venosa -> Erectile dysfunction -> Intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs sensitivity -> 80%
enhanced_information: Intracavernous injection of vasoactive drugs is more sensitive in erectile dysfunction related to venous causes compared to arterial, neurogenic, or hormonal causes. This is supported by the fact that venous causes of erectile dysfunction are more likely to respond to vasoactive drugs, as evidenced by the higher sensitivity observed in this group.
